content:
Nuevo Laredo is making it easy to get protected before respiratory-illness season. The city government will run a free two-day vaccination drive against influenza, pneumococcus and COVID-19 on Oct. 23 and 24, open to everyone six months and older, according to CML Noticias.

The drive runs from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. at the Esteban Baca Calderón plaza on Avenida Guerrero, between Héroe de Nacataz and Maclovio Herrera. Vaccination will be offered drive-thru style, with space also set up for people arriving on foot or by public transit. Officials say there is no limit on the number of people per vehicle, so whole families can come together.

Social Welfare Secretary Liliana Arjona said the effort is part of the city’s fall-winter preventive health actions, aimed at making vaccines accessible and reducing respiratory-illness risks. “Nos estamos preparando para lo que son las enfermedades del invierno,” she said, adding that all it takes is the will to show up and get vaccinated.

For minors, officials recommend bringing the child’s vaccination card to keep their history current, though it is not required. Adults need to bring an official ID. Everyone vaccinated will receive a certificate.

The city expects to serve about 1,000 people per day, based on turnout at previous drives. More details are available through the official channels of the Social Welfare Secretariat and the Municipal Health Directorate.

title: Nuevo Laredo Rolls Out Free Two-Day Vaccination Drive for Flu, Pneumococcus and COVID-19
